episodes.156161: A cold front spawned a line of thunderstorms that produced gusty winds over northern portions of the tidal Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay during the evening hours.
episodes.156699: A trough aloft moving over the islands generated heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms.  Most of the heaviest precipitation fell over portions of Maui, Oahu, and the Big Island of Hawaii;  bringing small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  No significant injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.157627: A cold front moving into a very unstable airmass triggered severe thunderstorms.  Some of these storms produced very large hail across portions of West Central Texas.
episodes.158140: A cold front moved across the region from west to east during the afternoon on April 11th, leading to scattered thunderstorms. A few isolated instances of flooding occurred in northeast MD, but nothing widespread across the forecast area.
episodes.158231: A large mesoscale convective system propagating southward from the central Florida peninsula initiated a large outflow boundary that pushed southward throughout the Florida Keys.  Widespread gale-force wind gusts, especially across the coastal waters of the upper and middle Florida Keys, resulted.
episodes.158236: Scattered thunderstorms from a decaying mesoscale convective system preceded strong gradient winds associated with a mesoscale low pressure passage through the Lower and Middle Florida Keys.  Frequent gale-force wind gusts resulted in a large power outage impacting the Lower Florida Keys.
